summary: Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka. He later taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

Ian Mabbett (1939–2020) was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Oxford until 1963, he served as Reader in History at Monash University (~1965–2004) and Professor at Aichi Bunkyo University (2000).

Ian Reader (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate at the University of Leeds (1983). He held posts at the University of Stirling (~1989–1995), Lancaster University (~1999–2006), and the University of Manchester (~2006).

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who earned his PhD at the University of Peshawar (2001–2007) studying under Farid Khan, Taj Ali, and Ihsan Ali. He held posts as Professor and Chairman at Peshawar (2001) and Associate Professor at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (b. 1936) is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University until 1959. He held posts at Otani University Junior College (attested 1978) and Otani University (~1973–2004).

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Nishogakusha, Kokugakuin, Tohoku (~1952–1965), Seijo, and the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama (b. 1942) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kogen Mizuno at Komazawa University and Otani University. He served as an associate professor (1975) and professor (1985–2013) at Komazawa University.

Ichiro Numata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held posts as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a sinologist and historian. He studied under Jitsuzo Kuwabara at Kyoto University (~1922–1925), where he later held an academic post from approximately 1936 to 1965.

Ida Vassalini (1891–1953) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She earned degrees in philology at the University of Padua and philosophy at the University of Milan, where she later taught from ~1939 to 1953.

Ignatij Andreevich Kossovich (1808–1878) was a linguist who studied at Vilnius University and Saint Petersburg State University. He served as Professor of Greek at Polotsk Uniate Theological Seminary (1833–1835) and later at the University of Warsaw (Docent 1870, Professor 1872–1878).
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) studied at the Sapienza University of Rome, where he later served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

Ignác Goldziher (1850–1921) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Eötvös Loránd, Berlin, Leipzig (PhD ~1869–1870), and Leiden under Ármin Vámbéry, Emil Rödiger, and Heinrich Fleischer. He taught at Eötvös Loránd University from 1872, becoming titular ordinary professor in 1894.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1940). He held posts at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, Pravda, and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1960–1998).

Igor Dmitrievič Serebrjakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1935–1940). He taught at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1941–1947) and worked as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1961).

Igor Mikhailovich Reisner (1898–1958) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the Special Faculty of the Frunze Military Academy. He later held a post at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1950–1958).

Ihsan Ali (b. 1955) is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Peshawar, UCL Institute of Archaeology, and under Frank Raymond Allchin. He served as Director of KP Archaeology (~2002–2006) and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009).

Ikko Arai is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Komazawa University. Their teachers include Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

Ikuhisa Takigawa (b. 1968) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He is attested in 2002 as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.
Ikuko Tazaki is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. In 2017, she is attested as a special researcher at Otani University and a collaborative researcher at Kyoto University.
